title: A feeder generator that keeps its promises

blocks.text: A distribution utility (fictional) wants a test portfolio of feeders for its performance work, from a few hundred up to 100,000. Each feeder has a length (1 to 40 km), a number of customers (50 to 5,000) and the crew-days its inspection takes (2 to 20). The data will be pinned by a hash in tests and grown over time, so the generator has to keep four promises:

items: **reproducible:** the same `n` and seed give the same feeders, also in a new Python process whose `PYTHONHASHSEED` differs;
**prefix-stable:** the first 10 feeders of a 1,000-feeder portfolio are the 10-feeder portfolio of the same seed;
**seeds do not overlap:** seed 8 is not seed 7 shifted by one feeder;
**every value in range**, ids numbered `F00001`, `F00002`, ... in order.

blocks.text: Write `generate_feeders(n, seed)` in `feeders.py`, returning a list of `Feeder`. The helper `between(draw, low, high)` turns one `random()` draw of a `random.Random` into a whole number from `low` to `high`. Use only `random.Random` and its `random()` method (through `between`), as GridCap does, so the numbers stay the same across Python versions. The ranges allow fewer than a million feeders. About six lines.

cases.says: the same seed gives the same feeders, numbered F00001, F00002, ...
every length, customer count and crew size lies in its range, and the values vary
the first feeders of a larger portfolio are the smaller portfolio with the same seed
seeds 7 and 8 do not give the same feeders shifted by one position
a fresh Python process with a different PYTHONHASHSEED gives the same feeders

origin.section: One Shared Stream Ties Every Draw to Every Draw Before It

concepts: one seeded random.Random, drawing only random(), gives the same portfolio in any process
a stream per item, seeded so no two collide, keeps earlier items unchanged when the generator grows
